detail.a: For a given conscious energy per source, the flow that moves rises as receptivity and alignment rise (and as the gap narrows).
detail.b: The gap (or receptivity) is defined as the ratio of conscious energy per source across a path to the flow through it.

screen.situation: With conscious energy per source held fixed, S040 says the flow rises as receptivity rises, but S083 defines receptivity as that energy per source divided by the flow, so receptivity rising would require the flow to fall.

For the same positive conscious energy per source across a path, increasing its positive receptivity increases the flow according to S040 but decreases the flow according to S083's definition of receptivity as that fixed conscious energy per source divided by flow.

verdicts.situation: Holding conscious energy per source fixed while the flow increases: A says receptivity has risen, but B defines receptivity as energy-per-source divided by flow, which has fallen.
At fixed positive conscious energy per source, increasing receptivity increases flow according to A but decreases flow according to B's definition of receptivity as energy per source divided by flow.

detail.a: E squared equals momentum times Current squared plus Movement M times Current squared squared.

screen.situation: An entity with zero momentum and Movement M = 2 would have E squared = 2 x Current^4 by S041 but E = 2 x Current^2 (so E squared = 4 x Current^4) by S075.

For one state with nonzero momentum and nonzero Current C, S075 makes E squared equal to the square of Movement M times Current squared, whereas S041 adds a nonzero momentum term to that same squared quantity.

verdicts.situation: An entity with nonzero momentum: A gives E squared as a momentum term plus the Movement term, so E exceeds C² × M, while B fixes E as exactly C² × M.
With nonzero momentum and nonzero Current, A adds a nonzero momentum contribution to E squared, whereas B fixes E squared to the square of Movement M times Current squared alone.

book_hits.text: I'm not equating a number of joules, because the left side has no numbers. Putting one E in the middle says there aren't two separate energies in the universe. There's one energy, organized as realization on one side of the mirror and as actualization on the other. There's nothing to count on that side, so I don't call it multiplication. I read the sign as the product of. In a sum, one part can do the work while the other sits at zero. In a product, if either factor is zero, the whole thing is zero: no Movement, no conscious energy. The first C is the Current carrying the Movement: where you are in the flow. That's momentum, and it's yours. The second C is that carried Movement given back to the Current. That's energy, and it belongs to everything. Once is momentum. Twice is contribution. Physics has the same two steps: mc is a mass's momentum through time, and the second c is what that momentum is worth to the universe as energy. The Current is the front edge of what the whole has reached, the same for every Movement no matter how aligned it is. What's invariant is the rate. Rest energy is the reflection of C²M: the energy a Movement has by existing in the Current, even when it isn't changing in Vibration. Kinetic energy is the reflection of a Movement changing its Vibration, which is where Frequency and Appreciation live. On each side, momentum is what a thing carries through its own continuum: mass times velocity physically, Movement times Vibration over Expansion nonphysically. The entity property called Momentum is those two met at the crossing.

book_hits.chapter: Chapter 2 · The One Rule / Chapter 16 · Twelve Reflections
book_hits.text: What you have to know is whether the relationship keeps its shape or turns around. If it depends on resistance, so that more mass means more of something, flipping resistant to receptive turns it around: more Movement means less of that thing, or it gets easier instead of harder. If it's an identity or a definition, two names for one thing, the way mass is density times volume and force is mass times acceleration, there's nothing to turn around, even with mass in it; the terms reflect and the relationship keeps its shape. Time dilation and length contraction don't depend on mass in physics, only on how close you are to the speed of light, so there's no resistance in them to flip, and they keep their shape, reflected as the gap and the shrinking distance. Number eight is about how much energy it costs to speed a mass up as it nears light speed. That one has mass in it, which means resistance is at work. When you flip resistance to receptivity, number eight has to invert: physically, each next bit of speed gets harder; nonphysically, each next bit of alignment gets easier.

book_hits.chapter: Chapter 2 / Chapter 8 · Two Kinds of Evidence
book_hits.text: And the condition flips, as always: Force reads how hard you're pushed against resistance, Frequency reads how freely you're yielding to receptivity. Physically, what you feel is the floor, how hard you're held. Frequency, the reflection of mass times acceleration, reads how freely you're falling. Under a steady pull, what holds you and how fast you're speeding up always add up to the whole pull: all floor and no speeding up when you stand, no floor and all of it when you fall. Appreciation is how much of the pull you're letting move you: full in free fall, low while you hold. The falling man is the most aligned with gravity anyone can be, and he's the one who feels nothing but ease.

Distance is what resistance makes, and there is none on the nonphysical side, so the relationship turns over: every Movement shares the Current. The physical rule says the edge is unreachable. Its reflection says the edge is where you already are. The formula keeps its shape on both sides, and what turns around is what it reads. Harder becomes easier; unreachable becomes already there. Kinetic energy follows from force = mass × acceleration and the definition of work, which both keep their shape, so it keeps its shape too. As a cost that rises with resistance, its reading turns over, which is number eight. The relationship isn't rewritten. With no distance in it, the part that splits observers drops out, and every Movement shares the Current.

book_hits.chapter: Chapter 0 (sample: Note Before We Begin, Prelude, Chapter 1)
book_hits.text: Nowhere, and everywhere. It doesn't have a location. A location is a physical idea, and the Current isn't physical. It runs through everything. What lets you feel it is your own perspective. Your sovereign perspective, I'd say. Nobody can feel it for you, and nobody can feel it from where you stand except you. All any of us can ever know about the whole is the connection we feel with it. Everything else reaches us through that same perspective. People sometimes want me to prove the Current exists first and then talk about feeling it. I understand why. But it's a bit like arguing with water that it's wet. You're in it. The question is how much of it you let yourself feel. **You keep using that word, sovereign. What does it mean here?** It means you have your own point of view on the whole, one nobody else can have. It doesn't mean independence from the whole. Every one of us is fully inside it. Sovereignty is that each of us is inside it *from somewhere*, and nobody else gets to be there. That matters later, when we get to how you should treat other people. Everyone you meet has their own Movement, their own place in the flow, and nothing I want or feel entitles me to theirs.

layer_c.note: The book endorses C²M and identifies its physical reflection as rest energy. It distinguishes rest energy from kinetic energy, but does not state that the E in B is a different quantity from the E in A or restrict B to zero momentum. Thus it does not make both equations true for the same energy with nonzero momentum.

layer_c.quote: Rest energy is the reflection of C²M: the energy a Movement has by existing in the Current, even when it isn't changing in Vibration. Kinetic energy is the reflection of a Movement changing its Vibration, which is where Frequency and Appreciation live.
layer_c.note: B (E = C²M) is the rest-energy case, the zero-momentum term. A is the fuller relation that adds the momentum and kinetic contribution. Both hold at once. The passage doesn't write out the squared sum, but it separates rest energy from the energy of a changing Vibration, which is the split A needs.

screen.situation: The sentence C^2 x M = E is itself a complete reflected sentence built from the vocabulary (Current, Movement M, E), so S068 exhibits exactly what S056 says is unavailable.

verdicts.situation: A is a meta-claim about the vocabulary rather than a description of a situation; what counts as a 'complete reflected sentence' (and of what it would be the reflection) is not fixed, so whether B is such a sentence, and thus whether the two conflict, cannot be decided.
When C² × M = E is stated as the nonphysical side of the Present, B supplies a complete reflected sentence that A says is unavailable.

detail.b: E squared equals momentum times Current squared plus Movement M times Current squared squared.

screen.situation: For an entity with zero momentum and Movement M not equal to 1, S068 gives E = C^2 x M while S079 read literally gives E^2 = M x C^4, i.e. E = sqrt(M) x C^2, so the two assign different E to the same entity.
For a Movement with Current C = 1, Movement M = 1, and momentum = 1, S068 gives E = 1 whereas S079 requires E squared = 2.

verdicts.situation: An entity with nonzero momentum: A gives E = C^2 x M exactly, while B (E^2 = momentum x C^2 + M x C^4, as worded) gives E^2 differing from M^2 x C^4, so the two assign different energy E to the same entity.
The vocabulary does not fix a mathematical relationship between momentum, Current, Movement M, and E that would establish whether the two equations agree or disagree.
